rows.label: 后缀 (-面)

lesson.title: 后缀 -面: 上面 下面 前面 后面 里面 外面
lesson.summary: -面 attaches to position words to make a side or place word: 上面, 下面, 里面.
pattern: 上 / 下 / 前 / 后 / 里 / 外 + 面
body: 面 (miàn) is a suffix that makes a side or place word: 上面 (above), 下面 (below), 前面 (in front), 后面 (behind), 里面 (inside), 外面 (outside). After a noun it names a place: 桌子上面, 学校后面; with 在 it says where something is: 杯子在桌子上面. A 面 word can also stand alone: 外面很冷, 前面就是银行.
The contrast example uses 边: 小狗在门边. 边 makes place words the same way (门边, 桌子上边). 边 and 面 are different suffixes; learn each place word as a whole. A common mistake is 旁面: the word is 旁边, never 旁面.

examples.translation: The cup is on the table.
Mum is in the kitchen.

examples.reading: xuéxiào hòumian yǒu yí ge gōngyuán.
examples.translation: There is a park behind the school.
The puppy is by the door.

examples.reading: yǐzi xiàmian yǒu yì zhī xiǎo māo.
examples.translation: There is a kitten under the chair.
The children are playing outside.
The bank is just ahead.

rows.label: 方位名词 (左, 右)

lesson.title: 左 and 右: 左边 右边
lesson.summary: 左 and 右 name sides; add 边 to make 左边 and 右边.
pattern: noun (+ 的) + 左边 / 右边
在 + noun + 左边 / 右边
body: 左 (zuǒ, left) and 右 (yòu, right) name sides. To name a place, add 边: 左边, 右边. After a noun, with or without 的, they make a place phrase: 学校的左边, 超市右边, 我左边. 左边 and 右边 can also stand alone: 右边的那个人. After 往 the bare 左 or 右 is enough: 往左走, 往右看.

The contrast example uses 往: 我们往右转. 往 introduces a direction you move toward, while 左边 / 右边 name a place (在桌子左边). A place word follows 在; a direction word follows 往. A common mistake is 桌子左 for a place: say 桌子左边.

examples.translation: The bank is to the left of the school.
My home is to the right of the supermarket.
Please go left.
We turn right.
He sits on my left.

examples.text: 右边的那个人是我哥哥。
examples.reading: yòubian de nàge rén shì wǒ gēge.
examples.translation: The person on the right is my older brother.

rows.label: 动词重叠 (AA, A一A, A了A, ABAB)

lesson.title: Reduplicated verbs: 看看 问一问 看了看
lesson.summary: Repeat a verb to say an action is brief or casual: 看看, 试一试, 看了看.
pattern: V + V: 看看, 想想
V + 一 + V: 试一试; V + 了 + V: 看了看
body: Single-syllable verbs can be reduplicated to say do something a little or casually: 看看, 想想, 尝尝 (AA). A一A puts 一 in the middle: 试一试, 问一问. A了A puts 了 in the middle and tells a short past action: 看了看, 试了试. Two-syllable verbs repeat the whole word (ABAB): 介绍介绍, 学习学习; they never take 一 in the middle (介绍一介绍 is wrong). Verbs like 是, 有 and 在 do not reduplicate.
A了A is only for something that already happened, so it cannot be used in a request: 请你看一看, not 请你看了看.
The contrast example uses 一下 after the verb (请等一下). 一下 also makes an action brief, but the verb itself is not repeated: in 等一下 the verb is not repeated, although 等一等 is also possible.

examples.translation: Please take a look.
Ask the teacher.
He glanced at his watch.
Please wait a moment.

examples.reading: lái, chángchang wǒ zuò de cài.
examples.translation: Come and taste the dish I made.

examples.reading: nǐ gěi wǒmen jièshào jièshào ba.
examples.translation: Tell us a bit about it.

rows.label: 能愿动词 (可能)

lesson.title: 可能: maybe, possibly
lesson.summary: Put 可能 before the verb to say something is possible.
body: 可能 (kěnéng) says something is possible: 明天可能下雨, 这件事可能很难. It usually goes after the subject, but it can also start the sentence (可能明天下雨). It can be a short answer on its own: 可能.
Watch the negation: 可能不来 means may not come, while 不可能 means impossible: 他不可能来, 这是不可能的. Do not shorten 不可能 to 不可.
The contrast example uses 会, which says a skill or a future fact rather than doubt: 他会开车. 可能 tells the listener the speaker is not sure.

examples.translation: That is impossible.
It may rain tomorrow.
Is that possible?
He can drive.

examples.reading: tā jīntiān kěnéng bù lái le.
examples.translation: He may not come today.

rows.label: 离合词 (帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞, 跑步)

lesson.title: 离合词: 帮忙 游泳 跳舞 跑步
lesson.summary: These verbs contain their object; put 了, 个 or a duration between the two parts.
pattern: 帮 + 忙: 帮个忙, 请他帮忙
游 + 泳 / 跳 + 舞: 游了一个小时泳
跑 + 步: 跑了一会儿步
body: 帮忙, 游泳, 跳舞 and 跑步 are separable: 帮+忙, 游+泳, 跳+舞, 跑+步. Put 了, 个, a person or a duration between the parts: 帮我一个忙, 游了一个小时泳, 跳了一支舞, 跑了半个小时步. Used as one block they take no further object: 我请他帮忙.

The contrast example uses the plain verb 帮, which takes a person as its object: 妈妈常常帮我. 帮忙 already contains its object, so you say 帮我一个忙 or 帮我, never 帮忙我. The same goes for 游泳: 游泳 or 游了一会儿泳, not 游泳了一个小时.

examples.translation: I asked him for help.

examples.reading: tā yóu le yí ge xiǎoshí yǒng.
examples.translation: He swam for an hour.

examples.reading: tā tiào le yì zhī wǔ.
examples.translation: She did a dance.
Mum often helps me.

examples.reading: wǒ pǎo le bàn ge xiǎoshí bù.
examples.translation: I ran for half an hour.

examples.reading: nǐ néng bāng wǒ yí ge máng ma?
examples.translation: Can you do me a favour?

rows.label: 疑问代词 (为什么)

lesson.title: 为什么: why
lesson.summary: 为什么 asks for a reason; answer with 因为.
body: 为什么 (wèishénme, why) asks for a reason: 你为什么迟到了？ 他为什么不来？ It usually comes after the subject, but it can also start the question: 为什么他不来？ It can close a short question too: 这是为什么？ Do not add 吗: 你为什么不来吗？ is wrong.
The contrast example answers with 因为: 因为天气不好. 为什么 asks, 因为 answers; the answer is usually a reason clause, not a thing. Do not confuse 为什么 with 什么 (what) or 怎么样 (how is it).

examples.translation: Why are you unhappy?
Why is he not coming?
The teacher asked me why I was late.
Because the weather is bad.
Why is that?

rows.label: 人称代词 (自己)

lesson.title: 自己: self, by oneself
lesson.summary: A pronoun plus 自己 stresses that person: 我自己, 你自己.
body: 自己 (zìjǐ) follows a pronoun or a name to stress that person: 我自己, 你自己, 他自己 (I myself, by yourself). It can also be the object when it points back to the subject: 你要照顾好自己 (take care of yourself). With 的 it means one's own: 我自己的房间. A common saying: 自己的事情自己做.
The contrast example uses 一个人 (alone): 我一个人去医院 says nobody goes with me. 自己 says I do it myself rather than someone else doing it for me; the two often go together, but they are different words.

examples.translation: I go to school by myself.

examples.reading: nǐ zìjǐ zuò fàn, hǎo ma?
examples.translation: Cook for yourself, OK?
He washes his clothes himself.

examples.reading: wǒ yí ge rén qù yīyuàn.
examples.translation: I am going to the hospital alone.
You must take good care of yourself.

examples.reading: zhè shì wǒ zìjǐ de fángjiān.
examples.translation: This is my own room.

rows.label: 指示代词 (那么, 那样, 这么, 这样, 每)

lesson.title: 这么 那么 这样 那样 每
lesson.summary: 这么/那么 show degree; 这样/那样 show manner; 每 means every.
pattern: 这么 / 那么 + adjective / verb
body: 这么 (zhème, so) and 那么 (nàme, so) go before an adjective, or a verb of feeling, to show degree: 这么大, 那么努力, 那么喜欢. 这样 (like this) and 那样 (like that) describe manner: 这样做, 别那样说. 每 (měi, every) goes with a measure word and often with 都: 每个学生都…, 每天.
The bare 这 and 那 cannot do these jobs: 这大 and 那说 are wrong; you need 这么 / 那样.
The contrast example uses 很, a plain degree adverb: 这家饭店很贵. 这么 and 那么 say so much, often with surprise or pointing at something; 很 just gives the degree without that reference.

examples.translation: This apple is so big!

examples.text: 他学习那么努力，一定能考好。
examples.reading: tā xuéxí nàme nǔlì, yídìng néng kǎo hǎo.
examples.translation: He studies so hard that he is sure to do well in the exam.
Let us do it like this.
This restaurant is very expensive.

examples.reading: měi ge xuéshēng dōu yǒu yì běn shū.
examples.translation: Every student has a book.
Do not say it like that.

rows.label: 形容词重叠 (AA, AABB)

lesson.title: Reduplicated adjectives: 大大的 高高兴兴
lesson.summary: Double an adjective for a vivid, warm tone: AA的 or AABB的.
pattern: AA + 的: 大大的, 红红的
AABB + 的: 干干净净的
AABB + 地 + verb: 高高兴兴地
body: Single-syllable adjectives can double to AA, usually with 的: 大大的, 红红的, 热热的. Two-syllable adjectives become AABB: 高高兴兴, 干干净净, 清清楚楚. A reduplicated adjective can be the predicate with 的 (房间干干净净的), go before a noun with 的 (一碗热热的面条) or before a verb with 地 (高高兴兴地回家).
Two-syllable adjectives are not doubled as ABAB: 干净干净 and 高兴高兴 are wrong as adjectives. A reduplicated adjective already carries degree, so do not add 很: 很漂亮 or 漂漂亮亮的, never 很漂漂亮亮 or 很大大的.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个书包很漂亮. 很 states a degree; reduplication paints a picture and sounds warmer or more casual.

examples.translation: Her eyes are big.
The room is spotless.

examples.text: 我们高高兴兴地回家了。
examples.reading: wǒmen gāogāo xìngxìng de huí jiā le.
examples.translation: We went home happily.
This schoolbag is very pretty.

examples.text: 他的字写得清清楚楚的。
examples.reading: tā de zì xiě de qīngqīng chǔchǔ de.
examples.translation: His handwriting is very clear.

examples.text: 我想吃一碗热热的面条。
examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng chī yì wǎn rèrè de miàntiáo.
examples.translation: I would like a bowl of nice hot noodles.

rows.label: 数词 (万, 好多, 多)

lesson.title: Numbers: 万 好多 多
lesson.summary: 万 is ten thousand; 好多 means a lot of; 多 after a round number means more than.
pattern: round number + 多 + measure / 岁
body: 万 (wàn) is ten thousand: 一万, 三万块钱; Chinese counts large numbers in 万, so 30,000 is 三万. 好多 (hǎoduō) means a lot of and goes before the noun: 好多人, 好多问题. 多 (duō) after a round number means a little more than: 四十多岁 (forty-odd), 一百多块.
多 cannot stand alone before a noun: say 很多人 or 好多人, not 多人. Also put 多 after the round number, not before it: 四十多岁, not 多四十岁.
The contrast example uses 几, which asks for a small number and needs a measure word: 你有几个朋友？ 几 asks how many; 多 after a number tells an approximate amount.

examples.text: 我们学校有一万个学生。
examples.reading: wǒmen xuéxiào yǒu yí wàn ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: Our school has ten thousand students.
There are lots of people in the park.
My dad is in his forties.
How many friends do you have?

examples.reading: zhè liàng chē sān wàn kuài qián.
examples.translation: This car costs thirty thousand kuai.

examples.reading: wǒ yǒu hǎoduō wèntí xiǎng wèn nǐ.
examples.translation: I have a lot of questions to ask you.

rows.label: 名量词 (条, 位, 间, 名; 借用 包)

lesson.title: Measure words: 条 位 间 名 包
lesson.summary: 条 for long things, 位 politely for people, 间 for rooms, 名 for roles, 包 for bags.
pattern: numeral + 条 / 位 / 间 / 名 / 包 + noun
body: 条 (tiáo) counts long, thin things: 一条鱼, 一条路, 一条裤子. 位 (wèi) counts people politely: 一位老师, 两位朋友. 间 (jiān) counts rooms: 一间教室, 三间卧室. 名 (míng) counts people in roles: 一名学生, 两名医生. 包 (bāo) is borrowed from the bag or packet: 一包饼干, 一包茶.

The contrast example uses 个, the general measure from Level 1: 我有一个书包. Use a specific measure when the noun calls for one, and learn the noun and its measure together: 一本书, 一件衣服, 一张纸 are not interchangeable.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le yì tiáo yú.
examples.translation: He bought a fish.
She is a teacher.
He is a doctor.
I have a schoolbag.

examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu sān jiān wòshì.
examples.translation: My home has three bedrooms.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yì bāo bǐnggān.
examples.translation: I bought a packet of biscuits.

rows.label: 动量词 (次)

lesson.title: 次: times, occasions
lesson.summary: 次 counts how many times: 一次, 两次, 三次.
body: 次 (cì) counts occasions: 一次 (once), 两次 (twice), 三次 (three times). Put the number and 次 after the verb: 打了两次电话, 一个月回一次家. With 过 it counts past experiences: 我去过一次北京. With a place or a thing as object, number + 次 can stand before or after it (去过一次北京, 去过北京一次); a pronoun object comes first (见过他两次).
次 does not count how long; use a duration such as 一个小时 for that. In a separable verb, 次 goes between the parts: 见过一次面.
The contrast example uses 一下: 我们休息一下吧. 一下 makes an action brief and is not counted; 次 counts the number of times.

examples.reading: wǒ qù guo yí cì Běijīng.
examples.translation: I have been to Beijing once.

examples.reading: tā kàn le liǎng cì zhè bù diànyǐng.
examples.translation: He watched this film twice.

examples.reading: wǒmen jiàn guo yí cì miàn.
examples.translation: We have met once.
Let us take a short rest.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi tā dǎ le liǎng cì diànhuà.
examples.translation: I phoned him twice.

examples.reading: tā yí ge yuè huí yí cì jiā.
examples.translation: He goes home once a month.

rows.label: 程度副词 (多, 好, 最)

lesson.title: 多 好 最: exclamation and superlative
lesson.summary: 多 and 好 exclaim before an adjective; 最 picks the highest degree.
body: 多 (duō) before an adjective makes an exclamation, usually with 啊: 多甜啊, 多美啊！ 好 (hǎo) in exclamations means so: 好冷啊, 这里的夏天好热啊！ 最 (zuì, most) makes the superlative: 最高, 最喜欢. Do not put 很 before 最, and do not use 第 for most: 第高 is wrong; 第 only counts order (第一).
The contrast example uses 很: 这个公园很大. 很 states a degree without exclaiming; 多 and 好 carry feeling, and 最 compares one thing with all others.

examples.translation: How sweet this watermelon is!

examples.reading: nǐ de fángjiān hǎo dà a!
examples.translation: Your room is so big!

examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì gāo de.
examples.translation: He is the tallest in our class.
This park is very big.
I like dumplings best.

examples.reading: zhèlǐ de xiàtiān hǎo rè a!
examples.translation: Summer here is so hot!

rows.label: 范围副词 (一起)

lesson.title: 一起: together
lesson.summary: 一起 goes after the subject and before the verb to say people do something together.
pattern: A 和 B + 一起 + verb
body: 一起 (yìqǐ, together) stands after the subject and before the verb: 我们一起吃早饭. With two people, join them with 和: 我和爸爸一起看电视. It is an adverb, so it goes before the verb: 我们一起吃饭, not 我们吃饭一起.
The contrast example uses 和 alone: 我和妹妹一起回家. 和 joins two people into one subject; 一起 says they act together. In 我和妹妹一起回家 both are present, and the order of 我 and 妹妹 can be swapped.

examples.translation: We eat breakfast together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé bàba yìqǐ kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: Dad and I watch television together.
The classmates go to the library together.

examples.reading: wǒ hé mèimei yìqǐ huí jiā.
examples.translation: My sister and I go home together.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng gēn wǒmen yìqǐ qù ma?
examples.translation: Would you like to go with us?

rows.label: 时间副词 (还, 已经, 有时(候), 快, 快要, 正)

lesson.title: Time adverbs: 还 已经 有时 快 快要 正
lesson.summary: 还 says still; 已经 says already; 有时 says sometimes; 快 / 快要 say soon; 正 says right now.
pattern: 有时(候) + clause; 快 / 快要 + … + 了
body: 还 (hái, still) says a situation continues: 他还在睡觉. 已经 (yǐjīng, already) usually has 了: 电影已经开始了. 有时 / 有时候 says occasionally and may stand before or after the subject: 我有时候去公园. 快 and 快要 say something is about to happen and need 了 at the end: 火车快开了, 快要考试了. 正 stresses the exact moment, often with 呢: 他们正吃饭呢.
正 and 快 do not mix with 了 the same way: 正…呢 is happening now, 快…了 has not happened yet, 已经…了 has already happened.
The contrast example uses 现在, a time noun: 她现在在开会. 现在 says when; 在 / 正在 / 正 are adverbs placed before the verb. Both 现在她在开会 and 她现在在开会 are possible orders.

examples.translation: He is still sleeping.
The film has already started.
I sometimes go to the park.
She is in a meeting now.
The train is about to leave.
They are eating right now.
The exam is coming up soon.

rows.label: 频率副词 (常, 经常)

lesson.title: 常 and 经常: often
lesson.summary: 常常 and 经常 before the verb mean often; 常 is the short written form.
pattern: subject + 常常 / 经常 + verb
body: 常常 (chángcháng) and 经常 (jīngcháng) mean often and stand before the verb: 我经常去图书馆, 他常常迟到. 常 is a shorter form, used mostly before a one-syllable verb: 常去, 常来玩儿. They describe a habit, not a single occasion.
In the negative say 不常 or 不经常; 不常常 is wrong: 我不常看电视.
The contrast example uses 有时: 她有时不吃早饭. 经常 / 常常 mean often; 有时 means sometimes, so the frequency is lower, and unlike 常 it can also start the sentence (有时她不吃早饭).

examples.translation: I often go to the library.
He is often late.
Grandfather often goes to the park.
She sometimes skips breakfast.
I do not watch television much.
You are welcome to drop by often.

rows.label: 否定副词 (别)

lesson.title: 别: do not, don't
lesson.summary: 别 before a verb makes a negative command: 别说话.
body: 别 (bié) is the spoken negative command: 别开门, 别去那里, 别忘了带书. It tells someone not to do something now or later.
The first contrast example uses 不要: 请不要在这里抽烟. 别 and 不要 both make negative commands; 别 is shorter and more spoken, 不要 is fuller and common in notices and writing.
The second contrast example uses 没: 上周我没去游泳. 别 cannot negate the past or a fact; for something that did not happen use 没, so 昨天我没去, never 昨天我别去.

examples.translation: Please do not open the door.
Do not forget to bring the book.
Do not go there.

examples.reading: qǐng búyào zài zhèlǐ chōu yān.
examples.translation: Please do not smoke here.

examples.reading: shàng zhōu wǒ méi qù yóuyǒng.
examples.translation: I did not go swimming last week.

rows.label: 关联副词 (再, 就)

lesson.title: 再 and 就 linking actions
lesson.summary: 再 says then / next after something else; 就 says then / as early as.
body: 再 as a connective says then, after something else is done; it looks to the future: 我先喝水，再吃饭; 吃完饭再走吧. 就 links a condition or a first event to what follows at once: 他一来我就走; 你想去，我们就去. After a time word 就 says early or soon: 我五点就起床.
For a repeated action in the past use 又, not 再; for a future step use 再, not 又: 吃完饭再走, not 吃完饭又走.
The contrast example uses 才: 他十点才起床. 就 says early or quick; 才 says late or not until, so 五点就起床 and 十点才起床 point in opposite directions. After 一 the partner is always 就, never 才.

examples.reading: wǒ xiān hē shuǐ, zài chī fàn.
examples.translation: I will drink some water first, then eat.

examples.reading: tā yì lái wǒ jiù zǒu.
examples.translation: As soon as he comes, I will leave.
I get up as early as five.
He does not get up until ten.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng qù, wǒmen jiù qù.
examples.translation: If you want to go, we will go.

examples.reading: chī wán fàn zài zǒu ba.
examples.translation: Eat before you go.

rows.label: 语气副词 (都, 就, 还是)

lesson.title: 都 就 还是: attitude words
lesson.summary: 都 stresses even; 就 stresses exactly or just; 还是 suggests or says still.
body: 都 adds emphasis, often with 了, meaning already or even: 他都十二岁了, 饭都凉了. 就 narrows or fixes: 我就想去公园 (that is all I want), 图书馆就在前面 (right there), 他就十块钱 (he has only ten kuai). 还是 suggests the better choice: 还是喝茶吧, 还是你先去吧.

The contrast example uses 也: 他也很想去. 也 adds one more person or thing. Do not confuse this with the 都 that means all: that 都 needs a plural subject (我们都去), while the emphatic 都……了 works with one person too (他都十二岁了).

examples.translation: He is already twelve.
I just want to go to the park.
Let us have tea instead.
He really wants to go too.
The library is right ahead.

examples.reading: fàn dōu liáng le, kuài chī ba.
examples.translation: The food has gone cold; eat up.

rows.label: 介词: 引出时间、处所 (从)

lesson.title: 从: from (time and place)
lesson.summary: 从 marks the start of a time or place span; 到 marks the end.
body: 从 (cóng) marks a starting point in space or time: 我从中国来, 他刚从学校回来, 我们从八点开始上课. It is often paired with 到: 从家到学校很近; with a verb in between it marks a whole span: 他从早上工作到晚上.
Do not use 在 or 往 for a starting point: 我在中国来 and 他往学校回来 are wrong.
The contrast example uses 在: 我的手机在包里. 从 introduces where something starts or comes from; 在 says where it is.

examples.translation: I come from China.

examples.reading: tā cóng zǎoshang gōngzuò dào wǎnshang.
examples.translation: He works from morning till night.

examples.reading: cóng jiā dào xuéxiào hěn jìn.
examples.translation: Home is very close to school.

examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī zài bāo li.
examples.translation: My phone is in my bag.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng bā diǎn kāishǐ shàngkè.
examples.translation: Our classes start at eight.
He has just come back from school.

rows.label: 介词: 引出方向、路径 (往, 从)

lesson.title: 往 and 从: direction and route
lesson.summary: 往 says toward; 从 says by way of / through.
body: 往 (wǎng) says toward a direction: 往前走, 往后看, 飞机往南飞. 从 (cóng) here says by way of or through: 我们从这条路走, 从公园里走过去. 往 is the direction you face or head; 从 is the route taken.
The contrast example uses 到: 我们到学校了. 往 points in a direction; 到 names the place you arrive at, so 到前走 is wrong.

examples.translation: Please walk straight ahead.

examples.reading: wǒmen cóng zhè tiáo lù zǒu.
examples.translation: We take this road.
Look behind you!
We have arrived at school.

examples.text: 我们从公园里走过去吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen cóng gōngyuán li zǒu guòqu ba.
examples.translation: Let us walk through the park.
The plane is flying south.

rows.label: 介词: 引出对象 (给, 比, 跟)

lesson.title: 给 比 跟: objects
lesson.summary: 给 introduces the receiver; 比 compares; 跟 introduces the person you act with.
pattern: 给 + person + verb: 给妈妈打电话
body: As a preposition, 给 (gěi) introduces the person who receives or benefits: 我给你介绍一下, 我给妈妈写了一封信. 比 (bǐ) introduces the thing compared: 我的书比你的多. 跟 (gēn) introduces the person you do something with or speak to: 请跟我来, 我想跟你说一件事. All three stand before the verb.

The contrast example uses 对: 他对中国文化很感兴趣. 对 says an attitude or interest is directed toward someone or something. 对 and 比 are not interchangeable, and in a 比 sentence the adjective takes no 很: 我的书比你的多, never 比你的很多.

examples.translation: Let me introduce someone to you.

examples.reading: wǒ de shū bǐ nǐ de duō.
examples.translation: I have more books than you.
Please come with me.

examples.text: 他对中国文化很感兴趣。
examples.reading: tā duì Zhōngguó wénhuà hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.translation: He is very interested in Chinese culture.

examples.reading: wǒ gěi māma xiě le yì fēng xìn.
examples.translation: I wrote a letter to Mum.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng gēn nǐ shuō yí jiàn shì.
examples.translation: I want to tell you something.

rows.label: 介词: 引出原因 (因为)

lesson.title: 因为: because
lesson.summary: As a preposition, 因为 + a noun phrase gives the cause: 因为这件事, 因为工作.
pattern: subject + 因为 + noun phrase + verb phrase
body: As a preposition, 因为 (yīnwèi) takes a noun phrase and gives the cause of what follows: 因为这件事，他很不高兴; 他因为工作没有时间休息; 他因为感冒没来上课. It can stand at the head of the sentence (with a comma) or after the subject.
With a noun phrase you do not need 所以. The usual mistake is to put 所以 here instead: 所以这件事 is wrong, because 所以 introduces a result, not a cause.
The contrast example uses the conjunction pair 因为……所以: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少. There 因为 introduces a whole clause and 所以 gives the result.

examples.text: 因为这件事，他很不高兴。
examples.reading: yīnwèi zhè jiàn shì, tā hěn bù gāoxìng.
examples.translation: Because of this matter he is very unhappy.

examples.text: 他因为工作没有时间休息。
examples.reading: tā yīnwèi gōngzuò méiyǒu shíjiān xiūxi.
examples.translation: Because of work he has no time to rest.
It is all because of the weather.

examples.text: 因为下雪，所以路上人很少。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià xuě, suǒyǐ lù shang rén hěn shǎo.
examples.translation: Because it snowed, there were few people on the road.

examples.reading: tā yīnwèi gǎnmào méi lái shàngkè.
examples.translation: He missed class because of a cold.

rows.label: 连词: 连接词或短语 (跟)

lesson.title: 跟 joining words: A 跟 B
lesson.summary: 跟 connects two nouns as a compound subject or object, like 和.
body: 跟 (gēn) can join two nouns or pronouns like 和: 老师跟学生, 爸爸跟妈妈, 我跟他. It is more spoken; 和 is the general form. The two joined words can usually swap places. Do not use 跟 or 和 to join clauses; use a clause conjunction such as 但是.
Do not mix it up with the preposition 跟 (跟我来): as a conjunction, the two nouns form one subject and often take 都.
The contrast example uses 和: 我家有一只猫和一只狗. 和 is neutral and common in writing; like 跟 it joins nouns, not clauses.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le miànbāo gēn niúnǎi.
examples.translation: I bought bread and milk.

examples.reading: bàba gēn māma dōu shì yīshēng.
examples.translation: Both Dad and Mum are doctors.

examples.text: 哥哥跟弟弟都喜欢踢足球。
examples.reading: gēge gēn dìdi dōu xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.translation: Both the older and the younger brother like playing football.

examples.text: 我家有一只猫和一只狗。
examples.reading: wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī māo hé yì zhī gǒu.
examples.translation: We have a cat and a dog at home.

examples.reading: wǒ gēn tā shì hǎo péngyou.
examples.translation: He and I are good friends.

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句或句子 (但, 但是, 那, 虽然, 还是, 因为, 所以)

lesson.title: Clause conjunctions: 但是 那 虽然 还是
lesson.summary: These conjunctions link clauses: 但(是) turns, 那 follows on, 虽然 concedes, 还是 offers a choice, 因为 / 所以 give cause and result.
pattern: 那 + clause; 虽然 ……，(但是 / 还是) ……
A 还是 B (choice); 因为 ……，所以 ……
body: 但 and 但是 turn to a contrasting second clause: 我很喜欢这本书，但是太贵了; 他很想去，但没有时间. 那 carries on from what the other person said: 那你就别去了. 虽然 concedes a fact: 虽然很累，他还是很高兴. 因为 gives a reason and 所以 the result: 因为太晚了，所以我打车回家.
As a conjunction 还是 joins two choices, also inside a statement: 我不知道他去还是不去. In such an embedded choice 或者 is wrong. (The 还是 in 虽然……，他还是…… is the adverb still.)

The contrast example uses 那 as a demonstrative: 那个人是我的老师. 那 before a measure word points at something (Level 1); 那 at the head of a clause is the conjunction then. The two 那 have the same shape but different jobs.

examples.text: 这本书很好，但是太贵了。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū hěn hǎo, dànshì tài guì le.
examples.translation: This book is good, but it is too expensive.

examples.reading: nà nǐ jiù bié qù le.
examples.translation: Then you had better not go.

examples.text: 我不知道他去还是不去。
examples.reading: wǒ bù zhīdào tā qù háishi bú qù.
examples.translation: I do not know whether he is going or not.

examples.reading: nàge rén shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: That person is my teacher.

examples.reading: tā hěn xiǎng qù, dàn méiyǒu shíjiān.
examples.translation: He really wants to go, but he has no time.

examples.text: 虽然很累，他还是很高兴。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn lèi, tā háishi hěn gāoxìng.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still happy.

examples.text: 因为太晚了，所以我打车回家。
examples.reading: yīnwèi tài wǎn le, suǒyǐ wǒ dǎchē huí jiā.
examples.translation: It was too late, so I took a taxi home.

rows.label: 结构助词 (得, 地)

lesson.title: 得 and 地: complement and adverbial markers
lesson.summary: 得 after a verb introduces a complement; 地 after an adjective marks how an action is done.
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of how the action turns out: 写得很好看, 来得太晚了. 地 (de) after an adjective or adverb marks how the action is done and stands before the verb: 慢慢地走过来, 认真地听. Both are read neutral.
Check what follows: a verb after the marker means 地 (快乐地唱歌); an adjective phrase after a verb means 得 (写得很好看). 慢慢得走 and 写地很好 are both wrong.
The contrast example uses 的: 这是哥哥的电脑. 的 comes before a noun and marks possession or description; 得 follows a verb; 地 comes before a verb. The same sound has three different jobs.

examples.reading: tā Hànzì xiě de hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: His Chinese characters are beautifully written.

examples.reading: lǎorén mànmàn de zǒu guòlai le.
examples.translation: The old man walked over slowly.
The children sing happily.
This is my older brother's computer.

examples.reading: nǐ lái de tài wǎn le.
examples.translation: You came too late.

examples.reading: tā rènzhēn de tīng lǎoshī jiǎngkè.
examples.translation: He listens carefully to the teacher's lesson.

rows.label: 动态助词 (过)

lesson.title: 过: past experience
lesson.summary: Verb + 过 says the action has happened at least once; negate with 没(有)…过.
body: 过 (guo) after a verb marks an experience in the past: 我去过中国, 你吃过北京烤鸭吗, 他学过两年汉语. To say it never happened, put 没(有) before the verb and keep 过 after it: 她没坐过火车. Do not use 不 here, and do not replace 过 with 了 in the negative: 没去了 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 了: 他喝了三杯水. 过 says someone has had the experience at some time; 了 says the action was completed on that occasion. 着 marks a lasting state and cannot express experience.

examples.translation: I have been to his home.

examples.reading: nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma?
examples.translation: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?
She has never been on a train.

examples.reading: tā hē le sān bēi shuǐ.
examples.translation: He drank three glasses of water.

examples.reading: tā xué guo liǎng nián Hànyǔ.
examples.translation: He once studied Chinese for two years.

rows.label: 动态助词 (着)

lesson.title: 着: continuing state
lesson.summary: Verb + 着 says a state holds or a posture continues: 门开着, 他拿着一本书.
body: 着 (zhe) after a verb marks a continuing state or posture: 门开着, 灯还亮着, 他穿着一件白衬衫, 他拿着一本书. It often describes a scene or background: 墙上挂着一幅画 (see 存现句).

The contrast example uses 在: 弟弟在做作业. 着 describes a state that holds; 在 / 正在 describe an action happening now. 门开着 is a state (the door is open), while 他在开门 is an action in progress (he is opening the door).

examples.translation: The door is open.

examples.reading: tā ná zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He is holding a book.

examples.reading: tā chuān zhe yí jiàn bái chènshān.
examples.translation: She is wearing a white shirt.
My younger brother is doing his homework.
The light is still on.

rows.label: 语气助词 (呢, 吧, 的, 啊)

lesson.title: 呢 吧 的 啊: sentence-final particles
lesson.summary: 呢 marks something going on; 吧 suggests; 的 confirms; 啊 exclaims or softens.
body: In a statement, 呢 (ne) marks that something is going on right now: 爷爷在睡觉呢. 吧 (ba) softens a suggestion or request: 我们走吧, 你先休息一会儿吧. 的 (de) at the end confirms with confidence: 他会来的. 啊 (a) adds feeling to an exclamation or softens a remark: 你的汉语说得真好啊！

The contrast example uses 吗: 你喜欢喝咖啡吗？ 吗 makes a plain yes-no question; 呢 / 吧 / 的 / 啊 each color the sentence differently and cannot replace 吗 there. Aspect words such as 过 and 着 are not sentence-final particles.

examples.translation: Grandpa is sleeping.
Let us go.
He will come.
Do you like coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ de Hànyǔ shuō de zhēn hǎo a!
examples.translation: Your Chinese is really good!
Have a rest first.

rows.label: 短语: 基本结构类型 (动补短语1)

lesson.title: Verb-complement phrases: V + result/degree
lesson.summary: A complement follows the verb and adds its result or degree: 看见, 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + complement: 看 + 见, 做 + 完
body: In a verb-complement phrase the second part tells what happens as a result of the action: 看见 (look and see), 听懂 (listen and understand), 吃完 (finish eating), 听清楚 (hear clearly). Negate it with 没: 我没听清楚. It is different from a verb-object phrase, where the second part is the thing acted on: 看书, 吃饭.
A result complement is not an aspect: 吃完了 says the eating is finished, 吃着 says it is going on.
The contrast example uses a verb-object phrase: 我想吃面条. In 吃面条 the second part is the thing (the object); in 吃完 it is the result (the complement), so 想完面条 is impossible.

examples.translation: I saw him.

examples.reading: tā yǐjīng chī wán fàn le.
examples.translation: He has already finished eating.
I understood.
I would like noodles.
I did not hear it clearly.

rows.label: 短语: 其他结构类型 (的字短语, 连谓短语, 兼语短语)

lesson.title: Phrases: …的, serial verbs, pivotal phrases
lesson.summary: 的字短语 stands for a thing; 连谓短语 chains verbs; 兼语短语 shares one person between verbs.
pattern: 请/让 + person + V (兼语短语)
body: 的字短语: 的 after a word or phrase stands for a thing or person: 我的, 红色的, 卖菜的 (the vegetable seller). 连谓短语: two verbs share one subject and happen together or in order: 去买菜, 去图书馆借书. 兼语短语: the object of the first verb is also the subject of the second: 让我帮忙, 请他来.
In a 的字短语 the marker is always 的, never 地 or 得: 卖菜的, not 卖菜地.
The contrast example uses 和: 我买了苹果和香蕉. 和 joins two nouns into one phrase; it does not chain verbs or make a pivotal structure.

examples.translation: I like the red one.
He goes to buy food.
Mum asked me to help.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo.
examples.translation: I bought apples and bananas.
The vegetable seller is here.
I am going to the library to borrow books.

rows.label: 短语: 功能类型 (名词性, 动词性, 形容词性)

lesson.title: Phrase functions: noun, verb, adjective
lesson.summary: A phrase can act as a noun, a verb or an adjective: 新书, 去买菜, 很大.
pattern: 名词性: 新的书 / 我的书
动词性: 去买菜 / 喜欢看书
形容词性: 很大 / 红红的
body: By function, a phrase can behave like a noun (名词性: 一件新衣服, 我的老师), like a verb (动词性: 听音乐, 学汉语), or like an adjective (形容词性: 很干净, 干干净净的). A verb phrase can even be a subject: 学汉语很有意思. Function depends on the head word and on where the phrase sits in the sentence.
The contrast example uses 的: 我的老师是北京人. With most nouns 的 is needed to make a noun phrase (我的书); kinship terms and institutions after a pronoun can drop it (我妈妈, 我们学校).

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn xīn yīfu.
examples.translation: I bought a new piece of clothing.
He likes listening to music.
This room is very clean.

examples.reading: wǒ de lǎoshī shì Běijīng rén.
examples.translation: My teacher is from Beijing.
Learning Chinese is very interesting.

rows.label: 固定短语 (什么的)

lesson.title: 什么的: and so on
lesson.summary: 什么的 follows a list to mean and so on: 苹果、香蕉什么的.
body: 什么的 (shénme de) closes a list, or follows one example, to mean and so on, and things like that: 他买了书、本子什么的; 我们去喝点儿茶什么的吧. It is informal. Because the list is open, the items of a longer list can usually be given in any order.
The contrast example uses 和: 我想买牛奶和鸡蛋. 和 links the items and closes the list; 什么的 adds and so on. Do not put 和 at the end in place of 什么的.

examples.reading: tā mǎi le shū, běnzi shénme de.
examples.translation: He bought books, notebooks and so on.

examples.text: 你可以带点儿水果什么的。
examples.reading: nǐ kěyǐ dài diǎnr shuǐguǒ shénme de.
examples.translation: You could bring some fruit or something.

examples.reading: tā xǐhuan dǎ lánqiú shénme de.
examples.translation: He likes playing basketball and things like that.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng mǎi niúnǎi hé jīdàn.
examples.translation: I want to buy milk and eggs.

examples.text: 我们去喝点儿茶什么的吧。
examples.reading: wǒmen qù hē diǎnr chá shénme de ba.
examples.translation: Let us go for tea or something.

rows.label: 固定格式 (还是……吧)

lesson.title: 还是……吧: a gentle suggestion
lesson.summary: 还是……吧 suggests an option after thinking it over: 我们还是走吧.
body: 还是……吧 makes a gentle suggestion or a choice after weighing things: 我们还是坐地铁去吧, 外面很冷，还是多穿点儿衣服吧. 还是 can stand after or before the subject (还是我们走吧). It softens advice; 吧 alone can also suggest, but 还是…吧 says this option is better.
The contrast example uses 好吗: 我们明天去，好吗？ 好吗 asks whether the listener agrees; 还是…吧 recommends one option instead of asking.

examples.translation: We had better go.

examples.text: 外面很冷，还是多穿点儿衣服吧。
examples.reading: wàimian hěn lěng, háishi duō chuān diǎnr yīfu ba.
examples.translation: It is cold outside; you had better put on more clothes.

examples.text: 路上车太多，还是坐地铁去吧。
examples.reading: lù shang chē tài duō, háishi zuò dìtiě qù ba.
examples.translation: There is too much traffic; we had better take the underground.
Shall we go tomorrow?

examples.text: 太晚了，还是明天再说吧。
examples.reading: tài wǎn le, háishi míngtiān zài shuō ba.
examples.translation: It is too late; let us talk about it tomorrow.

rows.label: 固定格式 (要/快要/就要……了)

lesson.title: 要……了: about to happen
lesson.summary: 要/快要/就要…了 says something is just going to happen.
pattern: 快要 / 就要 + V + 了
body: 要…了, 快要…了, 快…了 and 就要…了 all say an event is about to happen: 要下雨了, 火车快要到了, 他就要回来了. 了 at the end is required. 快要 is one word.
A time word can go before 就要 but not before 快要: 明天就要考试了 is right, 明天快要考试了 is wrong. Also do not use 正 here: 正…了 is wrong, because 正 is for something already in progress.
The contrast example uses 已经: 他已经回家了. 已经 says the event already happened; 要 / 快要 / 就要 say it has not happened yet.

examples.translation: It is going to rain.
The train is almost here.
He is about to come back.
He has already gone home.
The exam is tomorrow.

rows.label: 固定格式 (都……了)

lesson.title: 都……了: lateness or amount
lesson.summary: 都……了 stresses that something is later or larger than expected.
body: 都……了 stresses surprise or lateness: 都十点了，快睡吧; 他都十八岁了; 都快中午了，他还没起床. It sums up the scale and adds 了. This is not the 都 that sums people before the verb (我们都去).
The contrast example uses 已经: 我已经吃过了. 已经 simply says already; 都…了 adds surprise that it is so late or so much.

examples.reading: dōu shí diǎn le, kuài shuì ba.
examples.translation: It is already ten o'clock; go to sleep.

examples.text: 你都看了两个小时电视了。
examples.reading: nǐ dōu kàn le liǎng ge xiǎoshí diànshì le.
examples.translation: You have been watching TV for two hours already.

examples.text: 都快中午了，他还没起床。
examples.reading: dōu kuài zhōngwǔ le, tā hái méi qǐchuáng.
examples.translation: It is almost noon, and he is still not up.
I have already eaten.

examples.text: 这件衣服都穿了五年了。
examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu dōu chuān le wǔ nián le.
examples.translation: I have been wearing this for five years now.

rows.label: 主语 (受事主语)

lesson.title: Patient subjects: the thing comes first
lesson.summary: In a patient-subject sentence the thing receives the action: 作业做完了.
body: In a patient-subject sentence the subject is the thing the action happens to: 作业做完了, 这些衣服洗得很干净, 信已经寄出去了, 这本书我看过了. The doer can be left out because it is known or unimportant. This is not the passive with 被 (Level 3).

The contrast example uses the doer as subject: 我做完了作业. A patient-subject sentence puts the thing first (受事主语); an ordinary sentence puts the doer first (施事主语). Several orders are possible with the same words, so the word-order exercise is skipped for some of these examples.

examples.translation: The homework is done.

examples.reading: zhèxiē yīfu xǐ de hěn gānjìng.
examples.translation: These clothes have been washed very clean.

examples.reading: zhè běn shū wǒ kàn guo le.
examples.translation: I have read this book.
I finished the homework.
The letter has already been sent.

rows.label: 谓语 (名词性短语作谓语)

lesson.title: Noun-phrase predicates
lesson.summary: A noun phrase of date, age, price or weather can be the predicate directly: 后天星期五, 这个西瓜十五块钱.
body: With dates, weekdays, ages, prices and weather, Chinese often drops 是 and puts a noun phrase directly after the subject: 后天星期五, 我妹妹今年八岁, 这个西瓜十五块钱, 明天晴天. Adding 是 is also possible: 后天是星期五.
Two common mistakes: an ordinary noun of identity still needs 是 (他是老师, not 他老师), and the negative always needs 是: 今天不是星期天, never 今天不星期天.

The contrast examples use 是: 他是老师 and 今天不是星期天. 是 equates the subject with the noun and is required in the negative; the bare noun predicate is used only for date, age, price and weather and sounds more spoken.

examples.translation: The day after tomorrow is Friday.
This watermelon costs fifteen kuai.
Tomorrow will be sunny.
He is a teacher.
My younger sister is eight this year.
Today is not Sunday.

rows.label: 定语 (动词或动词性短语、主谓短语作定语)

lesson.title: Attributives: verb phrases and subject-predicate phrases
lesson.summary: A verb phrase or subject-predicate phrase can modify a noun with 的: 我买的书, 身体好的学生.
body: An attributive (定语) comes before the noun and usually takes 的: 我买的书, 昨天来的客人, 穿红衣服的人. A subject-predicate phrase can also be an attributive: 妈妈做的菜, 个子高的同学. Some short attributives drop 的: 汉语老师.
The contrast example uses 地: 他高兴地笑了. An attributive with 的 goes before a noun; an adverbial with 地 goes before a verb. Check what follows the marker, not just the sound: 我买地书 is wrong.

examples.reading: wǒ mǎi de shū hěn hǎokàn.
examples.translation: The book I bought is very good.

examples.text: 昨天来的客人是我的老师。
examples.reading: zuótiān lái de kèren shì wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The guest who came yesterday is my teacher.

examples.reading: māma zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: The food Mum cooks is delicious.
He smiled happily.

examples.text: 穿红衣服的人是我姐姐。
examples.reading: chuān hóng yīfu de rén shì wǒ jiějie.
examples.translation: The person in red is my older sister.

rows.label: 结果补语1 (错, 懂, 好, 会, 完)

lesson.title: Result complements: 错 懂 好 会 完
lesson.summary: A result complement after the verb says how the action turns out: 做完, 听懂.
pattern: V + 完 / 好 / 懂 / 会 / 错
body: 完 (finish), 好 (done well or ready), 懂 (understand), 会 (master a skill) and 错 (wrong) follow the verb as results: 看完, 做好, 听懂, 学会, 写错. 了 usually follows: 我学会游泳了. To say the result did not happen, use 没: 我没听懂. Inserting 不 or 得 (听不懂, 听得懂) says whether the result is possible.
The contrast example uses 得: 她唱得很好听. A result complement attaches the outcome directly to the verb; 得 introduces a description of manner or degree. Do not write 地 there: 唱地很好听 is wrong.

examples.translation: Have you finished reading it?

examples.reading: wǒ tīng dǒng lǎoshī de huà le.
examples.translation: I understood what the teacher said.
Dinner is ready.
She sings beautifully.

examples.reading: wǒ xiě cuò le yí ge zì.
examples.translation: I wrote a character wrong.
I have learned to swim.

rows.label: 趋向补语1: 简单趋向 (来, 去, 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过, 起)

lesson.title: Simple directional complements
lesson.summary: A one-syllable direction word follows the verb: 寄来, 上楼, 走进.
pattern: V + 进 / 出 / 回 / 过
body: 简单趋向补语 is one syllable after the verb: 来 toward the speaker, 去 away, 上 up or onto, 下 down or off, 进 into, 出 out of, 回 back, 过 across, 起 up. Examples: 跑上楼, 坐下, 走进教室, 跑回家. With a thing object, 来 / 去 can come before the object: 寄来了一封信.
With a place object, the place goes before 来 / 去: 走进教室来, 回家去; 进来教室 and 回来家 are wrong.
The contrast example uses the compound 上来: 他走上来了. A compound has two syllables (上 + 来); a simple complement has one (上 or 来). 跑上来楼 is wrong: a place object follows the simple 上.

examples.translation: He ran upstairs.

examples.reading: tā gěi wǒ jì lái le yì fēng xìn.
examples.translation: He sent me a letter.
He walked into the classroom.
He walked up here.
He ran home.
She sat down.

rows.label: 趋向补语1: 复合趋向 (上来, 下来, 进去, 出来, 回来, 过来, 起来)

lesson.title: Compound directional complements
lesson.summary: Two-syllable complements combine directions: 上来, 下来, 进来, 出来, 回来.
pattern: V + 下来 / 下去; V + 起来
V + 进来 / 进去; V + 出来 / 出去; V + 回来 / 过来
body: 复合趋向补语 combines a direction with 来 or 去: 上来 / 上去, 下来 / 下去, 进来 / 进去, 出来 / 出去, 回来 / 回去, 过来 / 过去, 起来. The second syllable points relative to the speaker: 来 toward, 去 away. Examples: 走进来, 拿下来, 跑出去, 走过去, 走回去, 站起来.

With motion verbs such as 走, 跑 and 站, a bare 进, 出, 回 or 起 does not normally end the sentence; use the compound form: 他站起来了 and 我们走回去吧, not 他站起了 or 我们走回吧 (下 is an exception: 坐下了 is fine). With a place object, the place goes between: 走进教室来.
The contrast example uses the simple 下: 他走下楼了. 下 alone takes the place object directly; 下来 is its compound form. Both describe movement, but 走下来楼 is wrong.

examples.translation: Mum walked in.

examples.text: 他从楼上拿下来一本书。
examples.reading: tā cóng lóu shàng ná xiàlai yì běn shū.
examples.translation: He brought a book down from upstairs.
He ran out.
He walked downstairs.

examples.reading: nǐ kuài zǒu guòqu kànkan ba.
examples.translation: Go over and have a look.
Let us walk back.
He stood up.

rows.label: 状态补语1 (动词+得+形容词性短语)

lesson.title: State complements: V + 得 + adjective
lesson.summary: 得 after a verb describes how the action is done: 说得很好, 跑得很快.
pattern: V + 得 + 很 / 非常 + adj
body: 得 (de) after a verb introduces a description of the action: 他跑得很快, 妹妹长得很高. This is different from a result complement such as 说完, and from an adverbial before the verb with 地 (高兴地说).
When the verb has an object, repeat the verb before 得: 她跳舞跳得很好, 他说汉语说得很流利. A common mistake is 他说汉语得很好; another is writing 地 after the verb (跑地很快).
The contrast example uses the result complement 完: 他说完了. 得 describes manner or degree; a result complement states the outcome directly.

examples.reading: tā tiàowǔ tiào de hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: She dances very well.
He runs very fast.
My younger sister has grown very tall.
He finished speaking.

examples.reading: tā shuō Hànyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
examples.translation: He speaks Chinese fluently.

rows.label: 数量补语2 (时量补语; 形容词+数量补语)

lesson.title: Quantity complements: duration and measurement
lesson.summary: Duration follows the verb: 住了两年; measurement follows an adjective: 大两岁.
body: Duration (时量补语) follows the verb, often with 了: 我在中国住了两年, 他等了一个小时, 我们走了半个小时. After an adjective in a comparison, a quantity states the difference: 他比我大三岁, 我的手机比你的贵一百块.

The contrast example uses 次: 我见过他两次. 次 counts occasions, not length; duration counts how long, and adjective + quantity measures a difference. With a pronoun object, number + 次 follows the pronoun (见过他两次, not 见过两次他).

examples.reading: wǒ zài Zhōngguó zhù le liǎng nián.
examples.translation: I lived in China for two years.

examples.reading: tā děng le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: He waited for an hour.

examples.reading: tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.translation: He is three years older than me.

examples.reading: wǒ jiàn guo tā liǎng cì.
examples.translation: I have met him twice.

examples.text: 我的手机比你的贵一百块。
examples.reading: wǒ de shǒujī bǐ nǐ de guì yìbǎi kuài.
examples.translation: My phone costs a hundred kuai more than yours.

examples.reading: wǒmen zǒu le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: We walked for half an hour.

rows.label: 单句 (主谓谓语句)

lesson.title: Subject-predicate predicates
lesson.summary: A whole subject-predicate phrase comments on the topic: 他身体很好.
body: In a 主谓谓语句 the predicate itself is a subject-predicate phrase: 他身体很好 (topic 他, comment 身体很好), 北京冬天很冷, 这件事我不清楚. The first noun is the topic, and the following subject belongs to it or is commented on in relation to it.

The contrast example uses an ordinary verb-plus-object sentence: 我喜欢汉语. A subject-predicate predicate comments on a topic; an ordinary sentence states an action with an object. 这件事我不清楚 can also be said as 我不清楚这件事.

examples.translation: He is in very good health.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì wǒ bù qīngchu.
examples.translation: I am not clear about this matter.
My mum is very busy with work.
I like Chinese.
Winters in Beijing are very cold.

rows.label: 疑问句 (还是选择问句)

lesson.title: 还是 choice questions
lesson.summary: A还是B? asks the listener to choose one of two options.
body: 还是 makes an alternative question: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？ 你今天去还是明天去？ The answer is one of the two, not yes or no, so do not add 吗 to the sentence. The two choices can usually be given in either order, except in a form like 你懂了还是没懂？, where the yes option comes first. In a question 或者 cannot replace 还是.
The first contrast example uses 吗: 你想喝茶吗？ 吗 makes a yes-no question; 还是 offers two choices. Choose the form that matches the answer you expect.
The second contrast example uses 或者 in a statement: 周末我在家看书或者看电视. In statements or means 或者; in questions it means 还是. Using 还是 in this statement is wrong.

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng hē chá háishi kāfēi?
examples.translation: Would you like tea or coffee?

examples.reading: nǐ jīntiān qù háishi míngtiān qù?
examples.translation: Are you going today or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ dǒng le háishi méi dǒng?
examples.translation: Did you understand or not?
Would you like some tea?

examples.text: 周末我在家看书或者看电视。
examples.reading: zhōumò wǒ zài jiā kàn shū huòzhě kàn diànshì.
examples.translation: At weekends I read or watch television at home.

rows.label: 祈使句 (别)

lesson.title: Imperative sentences with 别
lesson.summary: 别 + verb tells someone not to do something; 别…了 tells them to stop.
pattern: 别 + verb + 了 (stop doing it)
body: A negative imperative uses 别 (do not) before the verb: 别着急, 你别走！ The subject 你 is often left out but may stay. 别…了 tells someone to stop what they are doing: 别哭了, 别看电视了，快睡觉吧.
别 is only for commands. For a past fact use 没: 你没走 means you did not leave, which is a statement, not a command; 没着急 or 没哭了 as commands are wrong.
The contrast example uses 不要: 上课的时候不要说话. 别 and 不要 both command someone not to act; 不要 is fuller and more formal, while 别 is short and colloquial.

examples.translation: Do not worry; take your time.

examples.reading: bié kàn diànshì le, kuài shuìjiào ba.
examples.translation: Stop watching TV and go to bed.
Do not go!
Do not talk in class.
Stop crying!

rows.label: “是”字句2 (解释或说明)

lesson.title: 是 for explanation and characteristics
lesson.summary: 是 plus a quality or category explains what something is like: 这个苹果是甜的.
body: 是 can explain a characteristic or category, often with 的 at the end: 这个苹果是甜的, 这件衣服是毛的, 这张桌子是新的, 他是教书的. It states a fact about the subject rather than an action.
Do not confuse it with the 是……的 that stresses when, where or how a past event happened (我是昨天到的, Level 2 是……的句): here there is no event, only a description. 有 cannot replace 是 here: 这个苹果有甜的 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 很: 这个苹果很甜. 很 describes the degree; 是…的 affirms the quality as a fact or classification. They are close in meaning but not interchangeable in structure.

examples.translation: This apple is sweet.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn yīfu shì máo de.
examples.translation: This garment is made of wool.
He is a teacher by profession.
This apple is very sweet.

examples.reading: zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì xīn de.
examples.translation: This table is new.

rows.label: “有”字句2 (达到一个数量)

lesson.title: 有 + quantity: reaching a measure
lesson.summary: 有 plus a quantity says how deep, long or high something is.
body: 有 with a quantity states that something reaches an extent: 这条河有十米深, 这座山有一千米高, 我弟弟已经有一米八了. It says the thing reaches that measure. To ask, use 有多 + adjective: 你有多高？
The contrast example uses 很: 这条河很深. 很 only says the degree (very deep); 有 + quantity gives a measured amount, so 很十米深 is wrong.

examples.reading: zhè tiáo hé yǒu shí mǐ shēn.
examples.translation: This river is ten metres deep.

examples.text: 我弟弟已经有一米八了。
examples.reading: wǒ dìdi yǐjīng yǒu yì mǐ bā le.
examples.translation: My younger brother is already 1.8 metres tall.

examples.reading: zhè zuò shān yǒu yì qiān mǐ gāo.
examples.translation: This mountain is one thousand metres high.
This river is very deep.
How tall are you?

rows.label: 存现句2 (地方+动词+着+数量+名词)

lesson.title: Existential sentences: place + verb + 着 + noun
lesson.summary: A place plus a verb with 着 says something is there: 桌子上放着一本书.
body: Place words start the sentence, then a verb with 着, then the thing: 桌子上放着一本书, 墙上挂着一幅画, 门口站着一个人, 教室里坐着很多学生. 着 marks a state, and the thing after it is indefinite, so use 一本 / 一个 / 很多, not 这 / 那.
Do not put 在 after the verb in this pattern: 桌子上放在一本书 is wrong; 在 is used the other way round (书放在桌子上).
The contrast example uses 在: 妹妹在画画儿. An existential sentence describes what is at a place (a state); 在 + verb describes an action happening now.

examples.reading: zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yì běn shū.
examples.translation: There is a book on the table.

examples.reading: qiáng shàng guà zhe yì fú huà.
examples.translation: There is a picture on the wall.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí ge rén.
examples.translation: Someone is standing at the door.
My younger sister is drawing.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li zuò zhe hěn duō xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are many students sitting in the classroom.

rows.label: 比较句1 (A比B+形; A有/没有B+形; A比B+V+得+形)

lesson.title: Comparisons: A 比 B …
lesson.summary: 比 compares two things; 没有 says not as … as; with a verb use 得.
pattern: A + 比 + B + adj (+ 多了 / 一点儿 / 数量)
A + 没有 + B (+ 这么 / 那么) + adj
A + 比 + B + V + 得 + adj; A + V + 得 + 比 + B + adj
body: 比 (bǐ) puts the standard after it: 他比我高. After the adjective you can add the size of the difference: 今天比昨天冷多了, 我比弟弟大两岁. To say A is not as … as B, use 没有, often with 这么 / 那么: 我的房间没有你的那么大; to say A reaches B, use 有: 他有我这么高.
With a verb and 得, 比 B can come before the verb or after 得: 妹妹跑得比我快, 他唱歌比我唱得好. The most common mistake is adding 很 or 非常: 他比我很高 is wrong; say 他比我高多了 or 高一点儿. Also 跟 cannot replace 比: 他跟我高 is wrong.
The contrast example uses 一样: 他和我一样高. 比 shows a difference; 一样 says the two are equal.

examples.translation: He is taller than me.

examples.reading: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.translation: Today is much colder than yesterday.
I am not as tall as my older brother.
He is as tall as me.

examples.reading: mèimei pǎo de bǐ wǒ kuài.
examples.translation: My younger sister runs faster than me.

examples.text: 我的房间没有你的那么大。
examples.reading: wǒ de fángjiān méiyǒu nǐ de nàme dà.
examples.translation: My room is not as big as yours.

examples.reading: tā chàng gē bǐ wǒ chàng de hǎo.
examples.translation: He sings better than me.

rows.label: “是……的”句1 (强调时间、地点、方式、施事)

lesson.title: 是……的: emphasizing details of an event
lesson.summary: 是……的 stresses when, where, how or who did something: 我是昨天到的.
body: 是……的 emphasizes a detail of a past event: when (我是昨天到的), how (他是坐火车来的), where (我是在书店买的) or who did it (这个菜是妈妈做的). In the affirmative the 是 can be dropped; the 的 stays. Use it to answer when / where / how / who questions about an event that is already known to have happened.

The contrast example uses 了: 我昨天去了北京. 是……的 emphasizes the detail of a known event; 了 simply reports that the action was completed. Both 我昨天去了北京 and 昨天我去了北京 are possible orders, so the word-order exercise is skipped for that example.

examples.translation: I arrived yesterday.

examples.reading: tā shì zuò huǒchē lái de.
examples.translation: He came by train.

examples.reading: wǒ shì zài shūdiàn mǎi de.
examples.translation: I bought it at the bookshop.
I went to Beijing yesterday.

examples.reading: zhège cài shì māma zuò de.
examples.translation: This dish was made by Mum.

rows.label: 兼语句1 (请/叫/让+对象1+动词+对象2)

lesson.title: Pivotal sentences: 请 叫 让 someone do something
lesson.summary: 请/叫/让 take a person, and that person does the next verb: 请他来, 让我走.
body: In a pivotal sentence the object of 请 / 叫 / 让 is also the subject of the next verb: 老师请我们回答问题, 妈妈叫我早点睡, 医生让他多休息. Keep the order verb + person + action: 让他休息, never 让休息他.

The contrast example is a serial-verb sentence: 我去朋友家吃饭. There 我 does both actions (去 and 吃); after 请 / 叫 / 让 it is the person named who does the second action. That is why 让 cannot fill the gap in 我去朋友家吃饭.

examples.translation: The teacher asked us to answer the question.

examples.reading: māma jiào wǒ zǎo diǎn shuì.
examples.translation: Mum told me to go to bed early.
He let me leave first.

examples.reading: wǒ qù péngyou jiā chī fàn.
examples.translation: I am going to a friend's place for a meal.
The doctor told him to rest more.

rows.label: 双宾语句2 (主语+动词+给+对象1+对象2)

lesson.title: Double objects with 给: send someone something
lesson.summary: S + V + 给 + person + thing: 他寄给我一个包裹.
body: With verbs such as 送, 寄, 借 and 还, put 给 right after the verb and before the person: 他送给我一张票, 他借给我一本书, 他还给我五十块钱. The thing follows the person; 给 marks the receiver. 对 cannot do this job: 寄对我 is wrong.

The contrast example uses 把: 他把书给了我. The 把 construction (Level 3) moves the thing before the verb; the 给 double-object sentence keeps person and thing after the verb. In speech the thing can also come before 给 (他借一本书给我), so these sentences have more than one possible order.

examples.reading: tā jì gěi wǒ yí ge bāoguǒ.
examples.translation: He sent me a parcel.

examples.reading: wǒ jiè gěi tóngxué yì běn shū.
examples.translation: I lent a classmate a book.

examples.text: 朋友送给我一张电影票。
examples.reading: péngyou sòng gěi wǒ yì zhāng diànyǐng piào.
examples.translation: A friend gave me a cinema ticket.

examples.reading: tā bǎ shū gěi le wǒ.
examples.translation: He gave the book to me.

examples.reading: tā huán gěi wǒ wǔshí kuài qián.
examples.translation: He paid me back fifty kuai.

rows.label: 选择复句 ((是)……, 还是……)

lesson.title: Alternative complex sentences: 是……，还是……
lesson.summary: (是) A，还是 B offers two clauses as choices.
body: (是)……，还是…… joins two clauses as choices: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？ 我们是今天走，还是明天走？ It is the sentence form of the A还是B? question, and the answer is one clause.
The contrast example uses 吗: 你明天走吗？ 吗 asks for yes or no; 是…还是… asks the listener to pick one of two clauses.

examples.text: 你是在家看书，还是去图书馆？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zài jiā kàn shū, háishi qù túshūguǎn?
examples.translation: Will you read at home, or go to the library?

examples.text: 我们是今天走，还是明天走？
examples.reading: wǒmen shì jīntiān zǒu, háishi míngtiān zǒu?
examples.translation: Shall we leave today, or tomorrow?

examples.reading: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐfàn, háishi miàntiáo?
examples.translation: Would you like rice, or noodles?
Are you leaving tomorrow?

examples.text: 你是自己去，还是我们送你去？
examples.reading: nǐ shì zìjǐ qù, háishi wǒmen sòng nǐ qù?
examples.translation: Are you going on your own, or shall we take you?

rows.label: 转折复句 (虽然……, 但是……)

lesson.title: Concessive sentences: 虽然……，但是……
lesson.summary: 虽然 admits a fact, 但是 turns to the opposite result.
body: 虽然 (suīrán) concedes something; 但是 turns to the unexpected: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好; 虽然下雨了，但是他还是来了. 虽然 can stand before or after the subject (他的家虽然不大), and 但是 belongs at the head of the second clause. 所以 cannot be paired with 虽然.
The contrast example uses 因为…所以…: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了. 虽然…但是… links concession and turn; 因为…所以… links cause and result, so 因为 and 虽然 cannot replace each other.

examples.text: 虽然很贵，但是质量很好。
examples.reading: suīrán hěn guì, dànshì zhìliàng hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: It is expensive, but the quality is good.

examples.text: 虽然下雨了，但是他还是来了。
examples.reading: suīrán xià yǔ le, dànshì tā háishi lái le.
examples.translation: Although it was raining, he still came.

examples.text: 虽然他很累，但是还在工作。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn lèi, dànshì hái zài gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Although he is tired, he is still working.

examples.text: 因为下雨，所以比赛取消了。
examples.reading: yīnwèi xià yǔ, suǒyǐ bǐsài qǔxiāo le.
examples.translation: Because it rained, the match was cancelled.

examples.text: 他的家虽然不大，但是很干净。
examples.reading: tā de jiā suīrán bú dà, dànshì hěn gānjìng.
examples.translation: His home is not big, but it is very clean.

rows.label: 因果复句 (因为……, 所以……)

lesson.title: Cause and result: 因为……，所以……
lesson.summary: 因为 gives the reason, 所以 the result.
body: 因为…所以… links a reason and its result: 因为今天是周末，所以图书馆人很多; 因为妈妈病了，所以我没去学校. 因为 can stand alone in an answer, and 所以 introduces the second clause. Do not use 但是 for a result: 因为太累了，但是… is wrong.
The contrast example uses 虽然…但是…: 虽然他很忙，但是每天都运动. A causal sentence says one thing caused another; a concessive sentence admits a fact and turns against it.

examples.text: 因为路很远，所以我们坐车去。
examples.reading: yīnwèi lù hěn yuǎn, suǒyǐ wǒmen zuò chē qù.
examples.translation: Because it is a long way, we are going by car.

examples.text: 因为今天是周末，所以图书馆人很多。
examples.reading: yīnwèi jīntiān shì zhōumò, suǒyǐ túshūguǎn rén hěn duō.
examples.translation: Because it is the weekend, the library is crowded.

examples.text: 因为妈妈病了，所以我没去学校。
examples.reading: yīnwèi māma bìng le, suǒyǐ wǒ méi qù xuéxiào.
examples.translation: Because Mum was ill, I did not go to school.

examples.text: 虽然他很忙，但是每天都运动。
examples.reading: suīrán tā hěn máng, dànshì měi tiān dōu yùndòng.
examples.translation: Although he is busy, he exercises every day.

examples.text: 因为作业太多了，所以他很晚才睡。
examples.reading: yīnwèi zuòyè tài duō le, suǒyǐ tā hěn wǎn cái shuì.
examples.translation: He had too much homework, so he went to bed very late.

rows.label: 紧缩复句 (一……就……)

lesson.title: 一……就……: as soon as
lesson.summary: 一……就… links two immediate actions: 我一放学就回家。
body: 一……就…… says the second action follows the first immediately: 他一回家就睡觉了; 老师一说，我就明白了. The subjects may be the same or different; 一 stands right before the first verb and 就 right before the second. The partner of 一 is always 就, never 才.
The contrast example uses 先……再……: 我们先去超市，再回家. 一…就… stresses that there is no gap; 先…再… only lists steps in order.

examples.reading: wǒ yí fàngxué jiù huí jiā.
examples.translation: As soon as school finishes, I go home.

examples.reading: tā yì huí jiā jiù shuìjiào le.
examples.translation: As soon as he got home, he went to sleep.

examples.reading: tā yí kàn shū jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.
examples.translation: As soon as he starts reading, he feels sleepy.

examples.reading: wǒmen xiān qù chāoshì, zài huí jiā.
examples.translation: We will go to the supermarket first, then go home.

examples.reading: lǎoshī yì shuō, wǒ jiù míngbai le.
examples.translation: As soon as the teacher explained, I understood.

rows.label: 持续态 (动词+着)

lesson.title: 持续态: verb + 着
lesson.summary: 着 after a verb says a state continues or an action keeps going.
body: 着 marks that a state continues (树上挂着很多苹果, 床上躺着一只猫) or that an action keeps going (外面下着雨). V1 + 着 + V2 says how the second action is done: 他坐着看书, 我们走着去吧. It often describes how things are, especially a background scene.
The contrast example uses 在: 哥哥在打篮球. 着 presents a held state or continuation; 在 presents an action in progress at this moment. 在 cannot follow the verb in these sentences: 他坐在看书 is wrong.

examples.reading: shù shàng guà zhe hěn duō píngguǒ.
examples.translation: Many apples are hanging on the tree.
He sits reading.

examples.reading: chuáng shàng tǎng zhe yì zhī māo.
examples.translation: A cat is lying on the bed.
My older brother is playing basketball.
It is raining outside.
Let us go on foot.

rows.label: 经历态 (过)

lesson.title: 经历态: verb + 过
lesson.summary: 过 says someone has had the experience at least once: 我去过中国。
body: As an aspect, 过 says an action has been experienced at some time: 我爸爸当过老师, 你坐过飞机吗？ Negate with 没 and keep 过: 我没喝过中国茶, 我从来没见过这么大的西瓜. In the negative, 了 cannot replace 过 (没见了 is wrong).
过 stresses the experience; to simply report what happened on a given occasion, use 了 (我昨天去了北京). 过 can still appear with a time word when the point is the experience: 我昨天去过他家，他不在.
The contrast example uses 了: 下课了，我们走吧. This 了 says a new situation has begun; 过 cannot replace it, because the class ending is not an experience.

examples.translation: My dad used to be a teacher.
Have you ever flown?

examples.reading: wǒ méi hē guo Zhōngguó chá.
examples.translation: I have never had Chinese tea.

examples.reading: xià kè le, wǒmen zǒu ba.
examples.translation: Class is over; let us go.

examples.text: 我从来没见过这么大的西瓜。
examples.reading: wǒ cónglái méi jiàn guo zhème dà de xīguā.
examples.translation: I have never seen such a big watermelon.

rows.label: 数的表达法 (序数2: 数词+量词)

lesson.title: Number + measure: floors, classes, grades
lesson.summary: A number plus a measure names an ordered item: 二楼, 三班, 五年级.
pattern: numeral + measure (+ noun): 二楼, 三班
numeral + 年级 / 层 / 号
body: To name floors, classes, grades and rooms, put the number directly before the word, without 第: 二楼, 三班, 五年级, 四号房间. This is a label for an ordered unit, not a count of things: 三楼 means the third floor, not three floors.
Because it is a label, use 二, never 两: 二楼 and 二班, not 两楼 or 两班. (两 is only for counting: 两个人.)
The contrast example uses 第: 我的座位在第五排. 第 + number gives the position in a row or sequence; number + word names a fixed label such as a floor or a class.

examples.translation: My home is on the third floor.

examples.reading: wǒmen shì èr bān de xuéshēng.
examples.translation: We are students in Class 2.
I am in grade five.

examples.reading: wǒ de zuòwèi zài dì-wǔ pái.
examples.translation: My seat is in the fifth row.
Please come up to the second floor.

rows.label: 概数表达法1 (几; 数词+多+量词; 数词+量词+多)

lesson.title: Approximate numbers: 几, 十多, 一年多
lesson.summary: 几 gives a small approximate number; 多 after a number or a measure means more than.
body: 几 (jǐ) in a statement means a few or some (under ten): 我有几个苹果, 十几个男生. 多 after a round number means more than: 十多个学生, 两百多块. 多 after the measure means more than that many whole units, with a part left over: 一年多, 五个多月. Do not say 三个多人: people come only in whole units.
The contrast example uses 多少: 你们班有多少人？ 几 suggests a small amount and needs a measure word; 多少 asks about any amount and can go straight before the noun.

examples.translation: I have a few apples.

examples.reading: jiàoshì li yǒu shí duō ge xuéshēng.
examples.translation: There are more than ten students in the classroom.

examples.reading: tā zài Běijīng zhù le yì nián duō.
examples.translation: He lived in Beijing for more than a year.
How many people are there in your class?

examples.translation: This garment costs over two hundred kuai.

examples.reading: wǒmen bān yǒu shí jǐ ge nánshēng.
examples.translation: There are a dozen or so boys in our class.
